post.title: Travel scam losses nearly tripled since 2022
post.ig:
Americans reported losing $297 million to travel, vacation and timeshare scams in 2025, per FTC Consumer Sentinel data.
Reported losses in that FTC category: $104M in 2022, $122M in 2023, $274M in 2024, $297M in 2025. The big jump was 2024, when losses more than doubled while reports rose only about 6% (55,063 to 58,347). In 2025 there were about 64,300 reports.
The median reported loss in 2025 was $700, about 70% more than the roughly $415 median for all fraud.
The BBB says fake agencies push big package discounts, take payment upfront and vanish, and recommends confirming bookings directly with the hotel or airline. The FTC says a demand for wire, gift card or crypto payment is a scam sign and credit cards give the most protection; under the Fair Credit Billing Act you can dispute a charge for something not delivered, in writing, within 60 days after the first statement showing it.
Sources: FTC Consumer Sentinel Network data (2022-2025), FTC consumer guidance, BBB.
News and education, not financial advice.
